slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Parcelbird launch Parcelbird Now, its own 15-minute grocery delivery service, in 2027, given $12.0M of cash and a rule of 12 months of runway at all times?
Is quick commerce a market an operator can make money in?
Can Parcelbird Now earn a positive contribution per order by month 18?
Can Parcelbird fund the launch from current cash and keep 12 months of runway?
Is there a better use of the same cash?
What should the board decide in January, and what would make it reconsider?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
The board (two founders and two investors), approving or rejecting the launch
A path to profitability within the current $12.0M of cash, with no new round; At least 12 months of runway at all times; Positive contribution per order shown on evidence, not only on plan inputs
Board meeting, January 2027
A new funding round; Cities beyond the three; Partnering with operators

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Do not launch Parcelbird Now in 2027: at every observed level its stores lose money per order, and the plan breaks the runway rule; grow the software instead
Quick commerce sales nearly tripled from 2022 to 2025, but no operator has yet made it pay
–	Zipcart lost $1.90 and QuickBasket $3.40 an order in 2025
Parcelbird Now would lose money on every order unless it beats the best observed site on every input
–	The median site on our software loses $2.67 an order
–	The plan needs 3.5 orders per rider-hour; the best site gets 3.0
The launch does not fit the cash, even on the founders' own numbers
–	The plan falls $2.3M short of the 12-month runway rule at month 18
–	Nine sites at benchmark would lose about $18M a year
Growing the software is the better use of the cash and needs no new funding
–	Late-stage grocers alone would add a fifth to today's $4.1M ARR
–	Cash bottoms out near $5.4M, then grows from year three
Decline the launch in January, fund the software plan, and reopen only on evidence
–	Hire four people now; reopen only when a median site makes money after site costs
